description:
FILED s471a (Opus, 2026-09-06), by a #1273 probe.  PRE-EXISTING and NOT fixed
by #1273, deliberately.

    sub f { $_[0] = 9 }
    my @a = (1,2,3);
    f($a[-4]);

    perl 5.40.3 : dies "Modification of non-creatable array value attempted,
                  subscript -4 at â¦ line 1."
    PCL         : prints nothing, @a unchanged, exit 0

#1273 made every EAGER lvalue array accessor die for a below-start subscript
((setf p-aref), p-aref-box, p-array-set and the two autoviv element walkers).
`p-aref-argbox` -- the @_ argument accessor -- was deliberately LEFT quiet,
because it is the LAZY one and it also serves `%p-alias-aelem`, i.e. SLICE
reads and `values`, where perl is quiet:

    my @a=(1,2,3); my @s = @a[-4,-1];     # perl: (undef, 3), no die

So the accessor is asked one question by two call sites that want different
answers, and it currently answers the read one for both.  A fix has to
distinguish "this element is being aliased into @_ for a sub that may WRITE it"
from "this element is being read through a slice" -- which is the same
distinction `%p-defelem-box` already draws for a nonexistent-but-creatable
slot.  perl's own answer is that the DEFELEM carries the array and index and
dies at the WRITE, not at the alias, so the shape is probably a defelem whose
setter checks the index rather than a check in the accessor.

Two blessed rows sit behind it: `perl-tests/array.t` "error when setting alias
to negative index past beginning" and "â¦ to -1 elem of empty array"
(registered in cl/skip-registry.lisp under :principle9; the registration is
correct today and would leave with the fix).  See also #1305 for the
neighbouring stale entry in the same block.
subject: Writing through an @_ ALIAS to a below-start negative index is silently dropped where perl dies `Modification of non-creatable array value attempted` (p-aref-argbox is the LAZY accessor)
